definition: A contiguous sequence of n items (typically words or characters) from a given text, used in classical statistical language models.
details: N-gram language models, which estimate the probability of a word based on the preceding n-1 words, were the dominant approach to language modeling before neural network-based methods became practical and superior.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — N-gram — is what makes everything else possible.
